frontier.hypothesis: The duplicated-call form (7/211) is 3 instructions from target with target's register seat already correct; the gap is entirely GCC's cross-jump merge depth, and a source-level change to which block physically precedes the shared `jal func_8005C650` may flip jump.c:2005's shallow-merge preference so the deeper arm-to-arm merge at jump.c:2011-2021 runs instead.
frontier.mechanism: tools/gcc-2.7.2/jump.c:2005 calls find_cross_jump (insn, JUMP_LABEL (insn), 1, ...) first and only falls back to the sibling-jump loop at jump.c:2011-2021 when that returns newjpos == 0; the minimum=1 attempt currently succeeds on the one shared jal that the field67 path falls into.
frontier.next_probe: Compile the duplicated-call form with the pre-existing codegen-inert knob BB2_XJUMP_DEBUG=1 (tools/gcc-2.7.2/jump.c:66-89) and capture the XJDBG trace to tmp/grind/func_800747D8/s6/, then test whether reordering the selection_sound path relative to the field67 paths, or respelling the field67 calls so they no longer present a minimum=1 match at the shared label, changes the pairing decision.

frontier.hypothesis: The only clause of the store-flag transform a C author can still fail on a SINGLE-call spelling is tools/gcc-2.7.2/jump.c:1066 - the insn after the conditional jump must be followed immediately by the join label - and next_nonnote_insn does not skip a CODE_LABEL, so a genuinely-referenced label between the conditional jump and the constant store also fails it.
frontier.mechanism: tools/gcc-2.7.2/jump.c:1044-1066 sets TEMP to the 'x = b;' insn and then requires reallabelprev == temp or next_active_insn (temp) to be a simplejump to the same label; a second real insn in that arm, or a label preceding the store, breaks both alternatives.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate C shapes in which the zero arm is a shared join target for another real func_8005C650(0, 0x7F, 0x7F) site that already exists in this function (the ret>>16 case 1/case 2 arms, or the field67 case 1/2 blocks), so a referenced label legitimately sits between the conditional jump and the store. Do NOT add a statement that exists only to occupy the slot - that would be a dead-store/pad cheat and a first reach of an unsanctioned family.

frontier.hypothesis: Hunk 9's jtbl_80015A0C table-offset residual closes once the hand-transcribed array is deleted from src/text1a_b_mid_rodata.c in the same change that lands func_800747D8's real switch as committed C, mirroring the already-executed func_8006B578/jtbl_80015988 precedent.
frontier.mechanism: GCC 2.7.2 emits a switch's ADDR_VEC into the .rodata of the TU containing the switch; with the hand array still present in text1a_b_mid_rodata.c the sandbox's isolated single-function build sees a placement/offset conflict rather than the real target layout.
frontier.next_probe: At final-submission assembly time (not a src/text1b.c-only session): delete the jtbl_80015A0C array from src/text1a_b_mid_rodata.c in the same commit as func_800747D8's C body, then re-measure with sandbox --disable all --diff.
